title.en: India activist ends hunger strike after 26 days
title.zh: 印度活动人士在26天后结束绝食

summary.en: Sonam Wangchuk, a supporter of youth-led protesters demanding education reforms, says he wants to avert "possible violence".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
India's activist Sonam Wangchuk has ended a hunger strike after 26 days of fasting in support of youth-led protesters demanding education reforms.

In a post on X, Wangchuk - better known as "Sonam sir" - said he did so "after a long negotiation on various conditions" and also to avert "possible violence in the country".

Wangchuk, 59, went on strike to support the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), whose members also demand the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

The activist earlier said he had lost 11kg (24lb) but was "still alive". He was forcibly removed from a protest venue in Delhi last Saturday and taken to hospital.

Wangchuk, a well-known name in India, ended his hunger strike after the government assured him no legal action would be taken against protesters rallying at Janta Mantar site, India's NDTV website reported.

Reacting to Wangchuk's decision to end his hunger strike, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke wrote in a post on X: "We are relieved and grateful that Sonam sir has ended his hunger strike after 26 days."

But he added: "The Cockroach Janta Party's peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until [Education Minister] Dharmendra Pradhan resigns."

Mass protests have not stopped in the Indian capital, after the brutal police crackdown on Monday's march to parliament , which left scores of protesters and officers injured.

The CJP is now one of India's most visible youth movements. It is being seen as one of the biggest public displays of dissent against the government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's, which has been in power since 2014.

It emerged in May as an online satirical movement to protest against paper leaks and other irregularities in India's top exams and has gained a massive following on social media.

The protesters, who call themselves cockroaches, have been demonstrating for a month now, with some members also going on hunger strike.

They are demanding the resignation of the Education Minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, after a key entrance exam for aspiring doctors was cancelled in early May following a paper leak.
body.zh: 印度活动人士索南·旺楚克 (Sonam Wangchuk) 在禁食 26 天后结束了绝食抗议，以支持青年领导的抗议者要求教育改革。 在X上的一篇帖子中，旺楚克（更广为人知的名字是“索南先生”）表示，他“在就各种条件进行了长时间的谈判后”这样做了，也是为了避免“该国可能发生的暴力事件”。 59 岁的旺楚克举行罢工，支持蟑螂简塔党 (CJP)，该党成员还要求印度教育部长达门德拉·普拉丹 (Dharmendra Pradhan) 辞职。 这位活动人士早些时候表示，他体重减轻了 11 公斤（24 磅），但“还活着”。上周六，他被强行带离德里的一个抗议场所，并被送往医院。 据印度新德里电视台网站报道，在印度家喻户晓的旺楚克，在政府向他保证不会对在简塔·曼塔广场集会的抗议者采取法律行动后，他结束了绝食抗议。 针对旺楚克结束绝食的决定，CJP 创始人阿比吉特·迪普克 (Abhijeet Dipke) 在 X 上发帖写道：“索南先生在 26 天后结束绝食，我们感到欣慰和感激。” 但他补充说：“蟑螂简塔党在简塔·曼塔天文台的和平抗议将继续下去，直到[教育部长]达门德拉·普拉丹(Dharmendra Pradhan)辞职为止。” 周一前往议会的游行遭到警方残酷镇压，导致数十名抗议者和警察受伤，印度首都的大规模抗议活动并未停止。 CJP 现在是印度最引人注目的青年运动之一。这被视为对自 2014 年以来一直掌权的总理纳伦德拉·莫迪 (Narendra Modi) 政府最大规模的公开表达异议之一。 它于五月份出现，是一场在线讽刺运动，旨在抗议印度最高考试中的试卷泄露和其他违规行为，并在社交媒体上获得了大量追随者。 这些自称为蟑螂的抗议者已经示威一个月了，一些成员还进行绝食抗议。 5月初，由于试卷泄露，有抱负的医生的一项重要入学考试被取消，他们要求教育部长达门德拉·普拉丹(Dharmendra Pradhan)辞职。

title.en: Firefighters stand 'no chance' as European wildfires force tens of thousands to flee
title.zh: 欧洲野火迫使数万人逃离，消防员“毫无机会”

summary.en: Three firefighters have been killed as southern Europe endures more severe heat.

body.en:
Wildfires sweeping through parts of Italy, France and Spain on Thursday forced thousands of people to flee blazes fanned by scorching temperatures and strong winds.

Thousands of tourists on France's southern Atlantic coast have been forced out of campsites and holiday homes while Spanish authorities ordered another town near Madrid to evacuate late Thursday because of an out-of-control forest fire.

Three firefighters have been killed as southern Europe endures more severe heat, with temperatures topping 40C in some areas.

The total area of land burnt so far this year in European Union countries is the second largest on record, according to satellite data from the European Forest Fire Information System.

"The gendarmes came and knocked on every door, the fire was about 500 metres away — we grabbed some things and left," said Patrick Martineau, a 69-year-old resident of Le Porge, south of the French city of Bordeaux.

In Sicily, around 6,000 firefighters, forest guards and civil protection officers battled dozens of fires, some raging for several days, across the Italian island. One firefighter died after falling ill while battling the flames, the interior minister said.

Around Bordeaux, more than 20,000 people — mostly tourists in campsites and holiday lets — have been evacuated since Wednesday, as a fire ravaged a seaside pine forest.

"We're dealing with a very dense stand of closely packed pines," firefighter captain Wilfried Schneider told the Agence France-Presse news agency, describing a fire of "rare" intensity.

"We were on the beach and they told us to go back to the campsite to collect our things," said Belgian tourist Elke Urbain.

"We're not afraid because everyone is taking care of us, but we're sad for the people here."

Skies over Le Porge turned orange as smoke rose from charred and crackling pine trees, while helicopters made repeated runs over evacuated neighbourhoods.

Fires in 2022 damaged 30,000 hectares of the same forest, forcing some 50,000 people to be evacuated.

Fires are breaking out faster because of climate change caused by the burning of oil, coal and gas. European droughts are now more severe, climatologists from the World Weather Attribution group said in a study published on Thursday.

Across the border in Spain, authorities ordered 3,500 people in a town west of Madrid to leave their homes late Thursday because of a forest fire burning out of control.

Emergency services said alert messages had been sent to people in Aldea de Fresno ordering their evacuation.

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump said a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia depends on the kingdom recognising Israel — casting uncertainty over the agreement just the day after it was signed.

Saudi Arabia has long resisted joining the Abraham Accords , under which several Arab states established ties with Israel. The kingdom has long rejected joining the accords in the absence of a pathway toward Palestinian statehood.

The civilian nuclear deal announced on Thursday had appeared to be a major win for the Saudis, especially coming as Trump wages war on Iran in large part over concerns about the country's own atomic program.

But Trump threw a spanner into the works with his post on his Truth Social network saying the Saudi deal "will be approved, but is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords".

The White House said that the Saudis knew the deal was contingent on recognising Israel, although it was not mentioned when the deal was announced.

"The president is always the final dealmaker, as you know," White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt told reporters, adding that the Abraham Accords were "something that he feels very strongly about and has spoken about it in the past and will continue to uphold".

She said the US would "continue to have those conversations with our Saudi counterparts" to finalise a deal including recognition of Israel.

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said recognition by Saudi Arabia, a regional power and home to Islam's holiest sites, would mark a "historic leap" forward for peace in the Middle East.

Leavitt said she did not know of any calls between Trump and Netanyahu following the announcement of the Saudi agreement.

Should it go through, the deal to establish a civilian nuclear program in Saudi Arabia would generate billions of dollars for American companies, but with Trump's latest announcement, it was unclear whether it would ever see the light of day.

If the US "tries to force normalisation on Riyadh, it's not likely to work out very well", said H.A. Hellyer, senior associate fellow at the Royal United Services Institute for Defense and Security Studies.

"Would Saudi decide to do a complete 180 on what it has declared for the past three years, or 30 years? Quite dubious," he said.

Critics have also insisted that the deal could precipitate a nuclear race in a region already battered by war.

One provision would potentially see US companies build a uranium enrichment facility in Saudi Arabia, The Wall Street Journal reported.

title.en: Google and Tesla shares plunge as AI spending rattles markets
title.zh: 人工智能支出扰乱市场，谷歌和特斯拉股价暴跌

summary.en: As major tech companies race to capitalize on a new wave of AI technology, investors wonder when financial benefits will appear.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Shares of Google and Tesla plunged on Thursday as investors were spooked by the ever-increasing amounts of money being spent on artificial intelligence (AI).

Google's parent company Alphabet saw its share price drop by nearly 7%, while Elon Musk's electric vehicle-maker Tesla saw its stock fall 14.5%.

Both reported negative free cash flow - the money retained after paying for operations and investments - in financial results on Wednesday, alongside promises to spend billions more in the months and years to come.

It was the first time Google had seen the cash metric turn negative since it became a public company in 2004, according to its financial records.

As major tech companies race to capitalize on a new wave of AI technology, investors are wondering when financial benefits will show up.

Alphabet now expects to spend as much as $205bn this year, mainly on AI projects and infrastructure, a $15bn increase from a spending estimate it gave just three months ago.

Meanwhile, Tesla expects this year to spend up to $25bn on unspecified projects.

"There is still a healthy degree of scepticism about the ability of these investments to generate a commensurate level of return," Russ Mould, an investment director at AJ Bell, said.

Alphabet's combined quarterly revenue hit $119.8bn, up 23% compared with the same period last year.

Though Google parent Alphabet saw its business continue to grow in recent months, heavy spending on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure pushed its leftover cash into negative territory.

The company's free cash flow came in at negative $5.9bn (£4.3bn) for the first time in at least a decade, according to its past financial records.

Anat Ashkanazi, Google's chief financial officer, noted on a call with financial analysts that the company had recorded negative free cash flow due to growing capital expenditures, essentially all of which were related to AI spending.

She said the company spent $45bn in the second quarter, with 60% of the cost going towards servers and the remaining 40% going towards data centres.

Ashkanazi said on the call that when it comes to AI, "the demand still outpaces that investment".

"As long as we see these attractive opportunities to invest, we will continue to invest."

Sundar Pichai, Google's chief executive, said the technological shift to AI tools and capabilities still "feels like early innings in a shift across multiple areas" and the company's plans around generating financial returns on its spending were "disciplined".

"What I see with what you can do with frontier capabilities, there is still a lot of work left to do to translate that into experiences for our users. So that looks like extraordinary opportunities with extraordinary returns."

title.en: The US' $166 billion refund comes with a much bigger cost

summary.en: Trump's willingness to use tariffs to create persistent uncertainty signals a greater economic and legal danger.
summary.zh: 特朗普愿意利用关税制造持续的不确定性，这预示着更大的经济和法律风险。

body.en:
An Australian clothing company, Nashie, recently received a six-figure refund from the US government, including 6 per cent interest, for tariffs it had paid on US imports. It’s just one of thousands of businesses reclaiming tariffs imposed on what President Donald Trump called "Liberation Day".

Of the roughly US$166 billion (AU$237 billion) due to be refunded, more than US$85 billion (AU$121 billion) has already been returned to businesses.

But while a US Supreme Court ruling in February reversed the tariffs, much of the economic and political damage, and perhaps some of the Trump administration’s gains, will be hard to undo.

Trump’s April 2025 tariffs relied on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), a 1977 law that lets presidents respond to extraordinary foreign threats — yet never mentions the word "tariff".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

On 20 February 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled in a 6-3 decision that IEEPA did not authorise tariffs — under the Constitution, only Congress has the power to impose taxes and duties.

The decision placed an important limit on the president’s power to impose tariffs. But it did not end Trump’s tariff policy, which was, from the beginning, designed to buy time to rewrite US trade relations with the rest of the world.

Trump responded with a temporary 10 per cent global tariff, which expires on 24 July after the statutory 150-day limit.

Trump has also pursued more targeted tariffs under laws dealing with unfair trade practices, national security and anti-slavery claims.

These require investigations into foreign trade practices and lengthy procedures, which slow the process and also create a record that can be scrutinised in court.

The US Trade Representative’s findings on alleged forced labour have prepared the ground for a 12.5 per cent tariff on exports from 54 countries, including Australia, China, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, starting on 24 July 2026.

So while the Supreme Court closed one legal door, the Trump administration was already preparing to walk through another. And it has bought itself yet more time.

The refunds paid out contributed to a US$120 billion (AU$171 billion) federal deficit this June, in sharp contrast to the US$27 billion (AU$38 billion) surplus in June 2025.

That said, the US$166 billion (AU$236 billion) being paid out is not a fine. Much of it is money the government collected without legal authority and must now return. This is real money, but it’s less than 2 per cent of the projected 2026 federal government spending.

title.en: France evacuates 20,000 as wildfires spread in south-west
title.zh: 野火在西南部蔓延 法国疏散2万人

summary.en: Most of those evacuated were tourists from campsites around Arcachon Bay in France's Gironde region.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
About 12,000 people have been evacuated from the south-west of France and authorities are moving 8,800 others as wildfires spread in the Gironde region.

Local officials said some 3,400 hectares (8,400 acres) of land have already been destroyed around the Bay of Arcachon, as about 700 firefighters battle the flames.

Many of those who had to leave the area overnight were visitors to campsites on the Lège-Cap-Ferret peninsula.

Wildfires have also recently broken out in Spain and Italy. Several thousand people have been ordered to leave their homes in several locations west and south of Madrid, and a firefighter died after falling ill while tackling a blaze in Sicily.

The Gironde prefect, Sophie Brocas, said 10,000 visitors were among those evacuated from campsites overnight and the latest evacuations were going ahead "calmly" in the village of Claouey, on the shore of Arcachon Bay.

Brocas said no injuries had been reported. Some sites and roads were being closed in exposed forest areas.

"The work was relentless all night," said Gironde fire service chief Marc Vermeulen, who warned that temperatures were rising and the wind was getting stronger. "It'll peak at 20:00 [18:00 GMT]. Then we'll have to deal with... highly variable winds so we're currently tackling a fire that is going to be difficult to predict and that's why we cannot relax our guard."

Two local firefighters died earlier this week fighting another fire close to Bordeaux airport.

Yassmina de Freitas, 19, who lives in the coastal town of Le Porge, said she noticed smoke and the smell of burning at lunchtime on Wednesday.

By the afternoon "ash… [and] half-burned tree bark" were falling, the sky was "very dark" and the smoke was getting "thicker and thicker".

body.zh: 随着野火在吉伦特省蔓延，法国西南部约 12,000 人已被疏散，当局正在转移另外 8,800 人。 当地官员表示，阿卡雄湾周围约 3,400 公顷（8,400 英亩）的土地已被毁，约 700 名消防员正在与大火搏斗。 许多不得不过夜离开该地区的人都是前往雷日卡普费雷半岛露营地的游客。 西班牙和意大利最近也爆发了野火。马德里西部和南部多个地点的数千人被勒令离开家园，一名消防员在西西里岛扑灭大火时生病死亡。 吉伦特省省长索菲·布罗卡斯(Sophie Brocas)表示，一万名游客连夜从露营地撤离，最新的撤离工作正在阿卡雄湾岸边的克劳埃村“平静地”进行。 布罗卡斯表示，目前还没有人员受伤的报告。裸露森林地区的一些地点和道路被关闭。 吉伦特省消防局局长马克·韦尔默伦(Marc Vermeulen)表示，“整个晚上的工作都在无情地进行”，他警告说，气温正在上升，风也越来越强。 “它将在 20:00 [18:00 GMT] 达到峰值。然后我们将不得不应对……多变的风，因此我们目前正在应对一场难以预测的火灾，这就是为什么我们不能放松警惕。” 本周早些时候，两名当地消防员在波尔多机场附近的另一场火灾中丧生。 19 岁的亚斯米娜·德·弗雷塔斯 (Yassmina de Freitas) 住在沿海小镇勒波热 (Le Porge)，她说周三午餐时她注意到烟雾和烧焦的气味。 到了下午，“灰烬......[和]半烧焦的树皮”正在落下，天空“非常黑暗”，烟雾变得“越来越浓”。 当地时间 20:00 左右（英国夏令时 19:00），她的家人被执法人员疏散，并被带到邻近城镇的一家体育馆。他们不得不留下两只猫和四只鸡，因为在匆忙中找不到它们离开。 她说她根本无法入睡，每小时都会醒来检查火势的进展。 BBC 南方频道主持人乔·肯特 (Jo Kent) 与家人在法国度假，住在莱日 (Lège) 旁边的克劳埃 (Claouey) 的 Les Pastourelles 露营地。 她说，营地里许多对局势感到非常焦虑的人已经离开了。 肯特补充说，半岛南部的主要道路通常挤满了“从头到尾的交通”，但现在却空无一人，超市“安静得令人不安”。 在法国东南部的瓦尔地区，疏散的居民被告知他们可以在周四早上回家评估潜在的财产损失。然而，它警告人们限制在该地区的活动，因为随着风吹过，火灾可能会重新点燃……

title.en: Saudis must recognise Israel for nuclear deal, says Trump
title.zh: 特朗普表示，沙特必须承认以色列的核协议

summary.en: The US president says the landmark agreement to help Saudis develop nuclear energy is dependent on it joining the Abraham Accords.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The deal between the US and Saudi Arabia to help the Gulf kingdom develop nuclear energy is dependent on Riyadh recognising the State of Israel, President Donald Trump has said.

"The Civil Nuclear Deal (There will be no enrichment of material!)... which pertains only to non-military use... will be approved, but is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords," Trump said on Truth Social.

It was not immediately clear if the condition of joining the accords was stipulated in the text of the nuclear deal - which has not been released - or that Saudi Arabia had agreed to that condition.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said on Thursday that Trump had discussed the condition to Saudi leaders on numerous previous occasions.

"He has said if they don't join the Abraham Accords, the deal is off," she said. "So we'll continue to have those conversations with our Saudi counterparts moving forward."

Trump's comments come come after criticism from experts that the US-Saudi deal announced on Wednesday could run the risk of future nuclear proliferation in an already unstable region.

Some Republican and Democratic lawmakers expressed similar concerns, though Trump's Republican Party controls both the upper and lower chambers and opponents of the deal do not appear to have the votes needed to block it.

According to the US Department of Energy, it includes a "peaceful nuclear co-operation agreement" and a "bilateral safeguards agreement".

"Together, these two agreements lay the legal foundation for a decades-long, multi-billion-dollar partnership that advances several priority economic and strategic objectives, including nuclear nonproliferation," a statement from the department said.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said on Thursday that it was aware of US and Saudi plans for a "bilateral civil nuclear cooperation agreement and the plan to ask the IAEA to implement verification measures in relation to this".

"We look forward to receiving the request for such verification and to working with the US and KSA [Kingdom of Saudi Arabia] in ensuring the implementation of those measures."

During Trump's first term as US president, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Bahrain signed the Abraham Accords, resulting in a historic normalisation of relations between Israel and two Arab nations - the first in decades.

Saudi Arabia has previously said it will not do so without the establishment of a Palestinian state, but the White House said the deal would be off if Riyadh did not join the accords.

Posting on X, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said Saudi Arabia joining the accords "would be an historic leap forward for peace in the Middle East".

title.en: Ukraine's ousted defence minister insists on being reinstated
title.zh: 被驱逐的乌克兰国防部长坚持要求复职

summary.en: Mykhailo Fedorov refuses President Zelensky's offer to accept an alternative post, as the battle of wills continues.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Ukraine's ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has refused to accept an alternative post in Volodymyr Zelensky's government, insisting he wants his job back.

He thanked the president, but said there were "only three positions in the state - in addition to soldiers on the battlefield - which determine the course of the war: president, defence minister and commander-in-chief".

Zelensky said he had offered Fedorov several posts, including deputy prime minister.

Last week's removal of Fedorov - who is praised for transforming the armed forces - triggered mass protests. Zelensky was later forced to sack commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi, who conflicted with Fedorov.

Some protesters say the firing of Syrskyi is not enough, vowing to continue their street demonstrations until Fedorov is reinstated as defence minister.

Fedorov, 35, has been credited for using data to significantly improve the Ukrainian army performance on the front line and other innovations, including his successful Army of Drones initiative. He has also been praised for leading a drive against corruption.

Gen Syrskyi, 60, played a key role in the successful defence of the capital Kyiv during the first days of the Russian full-scale invasion in February 2022. But he is now seen by many in Ukraine as a Soviet-school commander reluctant to implement much-needed radical changes in the army.

In a statement sent to journalists on Thursday, Fedorov said his team had a "specific plan how to end the war" when he was appointed defence minister in January.

The key elements were the protection of the skies, stabilisation of the front, and also strikes against Russia's economy, he said.

"For six months, we have consistently implemented this very plan. For the first time in recent years, Ukraine has begun to seize the initiative [on the battlefield].

"Our collective results have created something unprecedented - a window of opportunity to force Russia into peace through strength. And we cannot afford to lose it."

He stressed that he had never been seeking any "post or status", but only wanted to have the "opportunity to really influence the result and bring Ukraine's victory closer".

Fedorov has already been replaced by Yevhenii Khmara, a former top official at Ukraine's Security Service (SBU).

Zelensky, who earlier this week had a meeting with Fedorov, revealed that he had offered him the post of deputy prime minister for military innovation.

"This is a very important role," the president said on Thursday, "because innovation must be co-ordinated with the leadership of the defence ministry, the commander-in-chief... and the president."

But Fedorov refused. It's not clear if his statement means that negotiations over his future are at an end.

title.en: US-Saudi nuclear deal: How will it impact Middle East, US-Iran war?
title.zh: 美沙核协议：将如何影响中东、美伊战争？

summary.en: Critics say the US-Saudi deal could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. It's certainly not making US allies, like Israel and the UAE, happy. And reports suggest the US may already be backtracking on the deal.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Critics say the US-Saudi deal could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. It's certainly not making US allies, like Israel and the UAE, happy. And reports suggest the US may already be backtracking on the deal.

After new statements by US President Donald Trump on Thursday morning, it is still unclear whether a controversial new deal with Saudi Arabia that allows the Middle Eastern autocracy to establish a civilian nuclear program will go ahead.

Trump said the deal could only progress if Saudi Arabia normalized diplomatic relations with Israel. In the recent past, the Saudi government has repeatedly stated it would only do this if the Israelis make genuine moves toward establishing a Palestinian state. With the current Israeli government, that is unlikely to happen.

The deal must also be voted on by the US Congress and there's been backlash already, with critics saying it could set off a nuclear arms race in the Middle East.

One of the main reasons experts are so worried is that in several years' time, the deal, as it stands now, may let the Saudis enrich their own uranium. The more uranium is enriched, the more it could potentially be diverted to make weapons. And in the past Saudi Arabian ruler Mohammed bin Salman has said that if Iran produces a nuclear bomb, then Saudi Arabia would need to have one too. 

The majority of the approximately 38 countries with civilian nuclear energy programs don't enrich uranium. Instead they import it.

The US-Saudi deal also has regional implications, especially because it seems to have been formulated in a far less rigorous way than similar deals.

The less strict deal the US has made with Saudi Arabia is likely to upset the  United Arab Emirates , who often compete with the Saudis for geopolitical influence.

The UAE already has a nuclear power plant, Barakah, as a result of arrangements made with the Americans back in 2009. 

As with almost all of the 26 nuclear cooperation agreements the US has, the UAE's deal also included what's known as an "additional protocol" signed with the International Atomic Energy Agency, or IAEA. This means the IAEA can thoroughly inspect all nuclear facilities. The UAE also agreed to forgo uranium enrichment.

The Saudi deal is bilateral only — that is, just between the US and the Saudis and doesn't include the IAEA — and the Saudis may eventually be allowed to enrich their own uranium.

summary.en: The latest US strikes on tunnels, bridges and other infrastructure further inland from the Strait of Hormuz could indicate that Washington is shifting gears in Iran.

body.en:
The latest US strikes on tunnels, bridges and other infrastructure further inland from the Strait of Hormuz could indicate that Washington is shifting gears in Iran.

With the US and Iran back at war following a prolonged but shaky truce , the latest US strikes seem to be less focused on Iran's coastal installations and maritime targets in the Strait of Hormuz .

Iranian media and local officials have reported  strikes on bridges, tunnels, roads, rail infrastructure, power facilities and desalination plants in southern Iran over the past week.

Hormozgan province, just north of the Strait of Hormuz, has been hit especially hard.

According to Iranian media, six bridges in Khamir county were struck early on Friday, July 17.

Hours later, more reports followed of attacks on two tunnels and two more bridges in Hormozgan. At least eight people were reported killed in the bridge strikes.

The US military also appears to have conducted the strikes in a very deliberate pattern. In the first wave, bridges west and north of provincial capital Bandar Abbas were hit.

In a second wave, another bridge to the east, one to the north and two tunnels north of the city were damaged. Alongside that, part of the railway west of Bandar Abbas was also struck.

Shukria Bradoost, an international security analyst at Virginia Tech in the US, told DW that the main US objective remains the same as before.

"The American goal in attacking southern Iran is to reopen the Strait of Hormuz," she said.

However, she noted that Washington is trying to do more than remove direct military threats to shipping .

The US military is destroying the infrastructure that could help Iran rebuild, reposition or sustain military pressure in the area, she added, noting that this was the reason that bridges, roads and rail lines have become targets.

She also warned that Washington could move to take control the strategic Kharg Island, the home of Iran's main oil export terminal, in its push to remove the wider threat to Hormuz.

The US has so far refrained from targeting energy facilities on the island, home to Iran's main oil export terminal, said Ahmad Vakhshiteh, director of the Moscow-based Center for Strategic Research on Developing Relations with the Middle East.

"Naturally, the island is valuable as long as its oil facilities remain operational and undamaged," he told DW. "But the key question is whether the United States is seeking to seize Kharg militarily or whether, through repeated attacks, it is pursuing what could be described as a political seizure of the island."

title.en: Trump's refugee policy: Only white South Africans welcome?

body.en:
Trump is spending more money on refugees, but it's mostly white South Africans who benefit. People from crisis-stricken countries are being denied entry. Experts say the credibility of US refugee aid has been damaged.

The US government cited an "unforeseen emergency" in South Africa  as the reason the refugee program would be expanded. However, only white minority South Africans — who are allegedly being persecuted on racial grounds in their country — would be granted refugee status . The Trump administration has repeatedly claimed that there is an ongoing genocide against white Afrikaners , allegations the South African government strongly denies .

Experts also say there is no statistical evidence of increased crime targeting white farmers. 

For Oscar van Heerden, a research fellow at the Center for African Diplomacy and Leadership at the University of Johannesburg, this is based on a distorted understanding intended to "undermine South Africa's moral authority on the international stage — by equating South Africa with the State of Israel."

Since the start of the war in Gaza , South Africa has been among Israel's harshest critics. In late 2023, Pretoria filed a lawsuit with the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague against the Israeli government over allegations of genocide against the Palestinian population in Gaza.

The case stems from Israel’s response to the October 7, 2023 terrorist attacks carried out by Hamas,  which is considered a terrorist organization by the US, the EU and others, and other militant Islamist groups. Israel denies the allegations of genocide and invokes its right to self-defense. It could take years before a final decision is reached.

Essentially, according to van Heerden, US President Donald Trump is saying: How can a country like South Africa bring Israel before the ICJ for alleged genocide against the Palestinians in the Gaza Strip when the South Africans themselves are committing genocide against white South Africans?

"He has this twisted notion in his head that he will convince the world that, after the Mandela years, we [South Africa] no longer have any moral authority in the world," he told DW.

Through an emergency order in 2025, Trump made it possible for members of white minority groups from South Africa to enter and resettle in the US . The US State Department's decision now calls for raising the annual cap on refugee admissions for the 2026 fiscal year from 7,500 to 17,500. The additional 10,000 spots are reserved exclusively for white South Africans. The State Department estimates that the expanded program would cost around $100 million (€87 million).

body.en:
Nearly four and a half years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of his country, Ukrainian President Volodymr Zelenskyy faces one of his toughest domestic political challenges yet.

In the past week, the biggest protests Zelenskyy's leadership has ever seen swept through Kyiv as frustrations over how to win the war against their eastern neighbour spilled over. Thousands of young people took to the streets to protest contentious recruitment methods and decry the allegations of corruption swirling around the administration.

In an effort to placate the demonstrators, Zelenskyy replaced his army chief Oleksandr Syrsky on Wednesday. The 60-year-old veteran commander had been the focus of the unrest following the removal of a younger, reform-minded defence minister.

That minister, 35-year-old Mykhailo Fedorov , was demoted by Zelenskyy just six months into the job. It has been reported that Syrsky may have encouraged Zelenskyy to get rid of the tech-savvy junior and has now himself been replaced by Mykhailo Drapatyi as head of the military.

Some believe that shift suggests Zelenskyy's leadership could be in trouble, especially given it comes after former prime minister Yulia Svyrydenko was replaced earlier this month.

Ukrainian opposition MP Oleksiy Goncharenko told  the SBS World News Weekly podcast  that Zelenskyy's position is "very weakened" amid ongoing corruption scandals, and the rotation of political appointments suggests Zelenskyy is trying to shore up his position.

However, Iryna Skubii, senior researcher in Ukrainian studies at the University of Melbourne, told SBS News that what may appear to be a crisis from the outside reflects "how democracy works" in Ukraine.

"It's how civil society illustrates what they want from political leadership at this time, and political leadership listened to them and made this decision accordingly," she said.

Ukraine has been subject to Russian aggression since the illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014. The conflict escalated when Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Skubii said Ukrainians are understandably tired but remain resolute in their rejection of Russian domination.

Peter Tesch, a former Australian ambassador to Russia, told SBS News that the divide between Syrsky and Fedorov — who is reportedly being considered for another position in Zelenskyy's government — is one between the old guard and the new. title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

reflection.en: In a world of intense technological competition and rising international tensions, the call to live peaceably with all people becomes profoundly relevant. Even amidst accusations and threats, seeking paths to de-escalation and mutual respect is vital for global stability. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to pursue peace wherever possible, even when faced with...
reflection.zh: 在科技竞争激烈、国际关系日益紧张的世界中，与所有人和平相处的呼召变得至关重要。即使面对指控和威胁，寻求缓和局势和相互尊重的途径对全球稳定也至关重要。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们，即使面对竞争，也要尽可能追求和平。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Democratic lawmakers propose bank funded by China tariffs to boost US manufacturing
title.zh: 民主党议员提议设立由对华关税资助的银行以提振美国制造业

summary.zh: 民主党议员提议设立一家由对华关税资助的银行，旨在为美国制造业提供拨款、贷款和投资。这项举措旨在振兴美国的工业腹地并支持小型企业。

A bill introduced this week would create a new bank to strengthen domestic manufacturing, provided with up to $15bn in funds each year. Continue reading...

reflection.zh: 当议员们提出振兴国家制造业和经济实力的策略时，这提醒我们，是雅伟赐予我们创造财富的能力。这种神圣的供应呼召我们以智慧和目标来管理我们的经济事业，认识到真正的繁荣最终来自祂。

verse.textEn: Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.
verse.textZh: 你要记念雅伟你的神，因为得货财的力量是他给你的。

title.en: Blocked by censors, China's animal lovers take fight against abuse offline and overseas
title.zh: 遭审查阻挠，中国动物爱好者将反虐待斗争转至线下和海外

summary.en: The killing of a dog and her puppies in Guangdong, China, has provoked widespread outrage both within the country and internationally. Animal welfare advocates, facing censorship, have taken their campaign against animal abuse offline and sought support overseas.
summary.zh: 中国广东省一只狗及其幼崽被杀害的事件，在中国国内外引发了广泛的愤怒。面对审查，动物福利倡导者已将他们的反虐待动物运动转至线下并寻求海外支持。

body.en:
When videos showing the horrific killing of a stray dog and her puppies sparked outrage on the Chinese internet in June, Beijing's censorship machine kicked into action.

But what was unusual this time was that it pitted the shocked and angry voices against authorities who said they were concerned about the four boys involved, all of them younger than 14.

China's Communist Party regime tightly controls media and the internet to suppress criticism of the state and to manage public anger. But in this case authorities cited the age of the boys as they urged people to withhold their comments and scrubbed social media posts about the incident.

"We urge the public not to disseminate related information, to reject cyberbullying, and to work together to create a good environment for the growth of minors," reads an official statement.

But the restrictions only seemed to spur the outcry. China's animal lovers have now taken their fight offline and abroad, even putting up billboards in New York to drum up support.

In China, posts about the incident are still drawing thousands of comments across social media, three weeks after the incident. There is shock, anger and sorrow, as well as demands for laws against animal cruelty, which China currently does not have.

Disturbing footage showing the boys in the city of Jieyang, Guangdong province, hitting three puppies with sticks before setting their mother on fire emerged online at the end of June. The boys were seen laughing as the dog, named Wang Wang, burned.

Jieyang authorities said last month that the boys would not face criminal charges and would instead be sent to a "specialised school", but did not elaborate.

Some reports suggest the boys filmed themselves and uploaded the video online, but police have not commented on that. Censors have tried to block the video to protect the boys' identity, although some people argue that it should stay.

Their identities have not been revealed, but snippets of the video with their faces visible continue to circulate online. There are also unverified posts claiming to be close-ups of the boys' faces, raising the risk of other children being wrongly identified.

Countries around the world restrict information about child offenders or set a high bar for identifying them.

For instance, media coverage and public access to juvenile court documents are often restricted to minimise psychological harm caused by undue publicity.

In this case, Chinese authorities have not completely banned the discussion yet. Keywords such as "Wang Wang" and "animal protection" came up as trending search terms on Monday, but posts related to them started to disappear towards the end of this week. Some users have also reported that their ability to share others' posts has been restricted.

body.zh: 六月，当一段显示一只流浪狗及其幼犬惨遭杀害的视频在中国互联网上引发公愤时，北京的审查机器开始了行动。 但这次的不同寻常之处在于，震惊和愤怒的声音反对当局，当局表示他们担心涉案的四名男孩，他们都不满 14 岁。 中国共产党政权严格控制媒体和互联网，以压制对国家的批评并控制公众的愤怒。但在这起案件中，当局引用了男孩的年龄，敦促人们不要发表评论，并删除了有关该事件的社交媒体帖子。 官方声明称：“我们呼吁公众不要传播相关信息，拒绝网络欺凌，共同为未成年人成长创造良好环境。” 但这些限制似乎只会引发强烈抗议。中国的动物爱好者现在已经在线下和海外开展了斗争，甚至在纽约竖起了广告牌来争取支持。 在中国，事件发生三周后，有关该事件的帖子仍在社交媒体上吸引了数千条评论。人们感到震惊、愤怒和悲伤，也有人要求制定禁止虐待动物的法律，而中国目前还没有这样的法律。 六月底，一段令人不安的视频出现在网上，显示广东省揭阳市的男孩们用棍棒殴打三只小狗，然后放火焚烧它们的母亲。当这只名叫旺旺的狗被烧死时，男孩们在大笑。 揭阳当局上个月表示，这些男孩不会受到刑事指控，而是会被送往“特殊学校”，但没有详细说明。 一些报道称男孩们拍摄了自己并将视频上传到网上，但警方尚未对此发表评论。审查机构试图屏蔽该视频以保护男孩的身份，尽管有些人认为应该保留该视频。 他们的身份尚未透露，但可以看到他们脸部的视频片段仍在网上流传。还有未经证实的帖子声称是男孩脸部的特写，增加了其他孩子被错误识别的风险。 世界各国都限制有关儿童罪犯的信息，或为识别儿童罪犯设定了很高的标准。 例如，媒体报道和公众查阅少年法庭文件往往受到限制，以尽量减少不当宣传造成的心理伤害。 在这种情况下，中国当局还没有完全禁止讨论。 “旺旺”和“动物保护”等关键词成为周一的热门搜索词，但与它们相关的帖子在本周末开始消失。一些用户还报告说，他们分享他人帖子的能力受到了限制。 它...

reflection.en: The outrage over the killing of a dog and her puppies highlights a deep human impulse to defend the vulnerable. Even when voices are censored, the call to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves, like these voiceless creatures, resonates powerfully. This reminds us of the biblical mandate to advocate for the rights of all who are destitute and...
reflection.zh: 对一只狗及其幼崽被杀害的愤怒，凸显了人类保护弱者的深层冲动。即使声音被审查，为那些无法为自己发声的无声生灵说话的呼吁，依然强烈地回响。这提醒我们，圣经要求我们为所有贫困无助、无法自卫者的权利发声。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: ‘A statement of freedom’: T-shirt slogan goes viral and book sales rocket in Taiwan after Hong Kong raids
title.zh: 香港突袭后，台湾“自由宣言”T恤走红，书籍销量飙升

summary.en: Taiwanese citizens express concern over the situation of independent booksellers in Hong Kong following recent arrests. A woman's defiant walk from a bookstore, wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with a "statement of freedom," has gone viral, leading to increased book sales in Taiwan.
summary.zh: 近几个月香港独立书商遭到一系列逮捕后，台湾民众对他们的命运表示担忧。一名女子昂首走出香港一家仅存的独立书店，她T恤上印着的“自由宣言”标语走红，导致台湾的书籍销量飙升。

body.en: Taiwanese people look on with concern at fate of Hong Kong’s independent booksellers, after series of arrests in recent months Walking out of one of Hong Kong’s last remaining independent bookstores, hands behind her back but head held high, the woman’s T-shirt was emblazoned with a simple slogan : “I am a bookstore employee”. Escorted by police, the woman was among five people arrested during raids on two bookstores last week , suspected of displaying and selling publications with “seditious” content, a national security crime which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾民众对香港独立书商的命运表示担忧，经历了近几个月的一系列逮捕事件后，这名女子背着手，昂首阔步地走出香港仅存的一家独立书店，她的T恤上印着一句简单的标语：“我是书店员工”。在警方的护送下，这名女子是上周在两家书店突击搜查中被捕的五人之一，涉嫌展示和销售含有“煽动性”内容的出版物，这是一项国家安全犯罪，最高可判处 10 年徒刑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In times when truth is suppressed, the simple act of seeking and expressing it can become a powerful statement of freedom. Yahweh's word reminds us that knowing the truth is intrinsically linked to liberation, offering hope even amidst challenging circumstances. This story highlights the enduring human spirit that yearns for truth and the freedom it brings.
reflection.zh: 在真相被压制之时，寻求和表达真相的简单行为可以成为一种强大的自由宣言。雅伟的话语提醒我们，认识真理与获得自由是紧密相连的，即使在充满挑战的环境中也能带来希望。这个故事凸显了人类对真理及其所带来的自由的持久渴望。

verse.textEn: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
verse.textZh: 你们必晓得真理，真理必叫你们得以自由。

title.en: The Guardian view on Chinese workers picking up the pen: poetry in motion | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》观点：中国工人拿起笔杆子，诗意盎然 | 社论

summary.en: A food delivery rider has won China's highest literary award, highlighting a growing trend of laborers engaging in creative writing. This phenomenon sheds light on the hundreds of millions who have built modern China, from street sweepers to factory workers and goods transporters, revealing their rich inner lives.
summary.zh: 一名外卖骑手荣获中国最高文学奖，这凸显了劳动者从事创意写作的日益增长的趋势。这一现象揭示了数亿建设现代中国的劳动者——从扫街工人到工厂员工和货物运输者——丰富的内心世界。

body.en: A food delivery rider has won the country’s highest literary award. It is part of a growing trend for writing by labourers The hundreds of millions who have built modern China from the ground up – sweeping its streets, labouring in its factories and ferrying its goods – are often overlooked. But they refuse to go unheard. Last week, a food delivery rider won China’s top literary award . Wang Jibing, 56, first caught attention when a poem about his experiences went viral in 2022. The following year, Hu Anyan’s memoir , I Deliver Parcels in Beijing, became a bestseller. In the early 20th century, Chinese intellectuals sought to capture the harsh realities of working-class lives. But it was under Mao Zedong that the idea of writing by as well as about the masses became reality, with labourers encouraged to take up the pen. In an era when the party tried to govern the language even of diaries and personal letters, the parameters of style and content were strict, and this enthusiasm swiftly diminished after Mao. body.zh: 一名送餐骑手获得了该国最高文学奖。这是劳动者写作日益增长的趋势的一部分。数以亿计白手起家建设现代中国的人——清扫街道、在工厂劳动、运送货物——常常被忽视。但他们拒绝被忽视。上周，一名外卖骑手荣获中国最高文学奖。 56 岁的王吉兵首次引起关注是在 2022 年，一首描写自己经历的诗在网上疯传。次年，胡安彦的回忆录《我在北京送包裹》成为畅销书。 20世纪初，中国知识分子试图捕捉工人阶级生活的严酷现实。但正是在毛泽东的领导下，由群众写作、为群众写作的理念才成为现实，并鼓励劳动者拿起笔来。在党试图控制日记和私人信件语言的时代，风格和内容的参数都很严格，这种热情在毛泽东之后迅速减弱。但工人写作在21世纪出现了复兴。这一次，它是自下而上的，而不是自上而下的。您对本文提出的问题有什么看法吗？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story reminds us that every person is Yahweh's handiwork, created with unique gifts and a purpose to do good works, often in ways that surprise us. It beautifully illustrates how creativity and dignity are not limited by one's occupation, but can flourish in any life dedicated to expressing its inherent worth.
reflection.zh: 这个故事提醒我们，每个人都是雅伟的杰作，被赋予独特的恩赐和行善的目的，其方式常常出人意料。它优美地阐明了创造力和尊严并不受职业限制，而是在任何致力于表达其内在价值的生命中都能蓬勃发展。

verse.textEn: For we are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.
verse.textZh: 我们原是他的工作，在基督耶稣里造成的，为要叫我们行善，就是神所预备叫我们行的。

title.en: Can India become the next semiconductor hub after Taiwan?
title.zh: 印度能否成为继台湾之后的下一个半导体中心？

summary.en: India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.
summary.zh: 随着主要工业强国寻求将供应链多元化，不再只依赖台湾，印度正投入数十亿美元建设国内半导体产业。

body.en:
India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.

More than 90% of the world's most advanced semiconductor chips are made in Taiwan , an island at the center of ongoing rivalry between the US and China .

Any disruption to Taiwan's chip industry would likely send shockwaves through the global economy, with modern semiconductors used to make everything from smartphones and electric vehicles (EVs) to aircraft and military systems .

During the COVID-19 pandemic, chip shortages forced automakers to halt production — exposing how dependent the world had become on a handful of manufacturers in East Asia.

The result has been a global race to build more resilient semiconductor supply chains. The US, Japan, South Korea and also the EU have all launched multi-billion-dollar programs to attract chipmakers.

India is now mounting its biggest push yet to become part of that network and enter the global arena as the next electronics powerhouse.

Last week, the Indian government approved a $13.2 billion (€11.4 billion) semiconductor program labeled Semicon 2.0. The project builds on the $9 billion India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) launched in 2021 and aims to develop the entire chip ecosystem — from chip design and fabrication to advanced packaging, specialty materials, equipment manufacturing and workforce training. 

Thousands of engineers working for companies such as Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and Texas Instruments already design some of the world's most sophisticated chips from research centers in the Indian cities of Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Noida.

But analysts warn India has been lagging behind in large-scale manufacturing. In the semiconductor industry,  this is the area that brings both economic value and strategic importance.

"India already has the expertise to design sophisticated semiconductor chips," said V Kamakoti, director of the Indian Institute of Technology in the city of Madras.

"Indian engineers working for both domestic companies and multinational firms have successfully designed and delivered complex chips," Kamakoti told DW. "The bigger challenge is manufacturing them."

So far, India's progress has been concentrated in chip packaging and testing rather than manufacturing the chips themselves.

Kamakoti said the next step is building a domestic fabrication ecosystem that can turn those design strengths into large-scale production.

Micron Technology, a US memory chip maker, Kaynes Semicon and CG Semi, two Indian semiconductor assembly and packaging companies, have begun commercial production under the first phase of India's semiconductor program.

title.en: 'Strong concerns': Australia meets with China following ballistic missile test

summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

A foreign ministers' meeting of the forum will be held in August, where the issue is likely to be discussed.

title.en: Not a 'one off spike': Why higher petrol prices are set to return
title.zh: 并非“一次性飙升”：为何汽油价格将卷土重来

summary.en: Multiple factors are expected to push up prices at the bowser, as markets also ramp up expectations for another rate hike.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Petrol prices are expected to rise once again, which could cause a crunch at the bowser for Australians already feeling the pinch.

While Australia's resilient labour market continues to be a bright spot in the nation's economy, including the addition of more than 76,000 jobs in June, dark clouds are gathering on the horizon.

After the Australian Bureau of Statistics released another strong labour force report on Thursday, bonds traders ratcheted up expectations that the Reserve Bank will raise interest rates for a fourth time in 2026.

The market is now full priced in for a rate hike by Christmas. A few weeks ago it was a 50-50 bet.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Renewed hostilities in the Middle East have sent oil prices rising again and threaten to add fresh inflationary pressures to the economy.

While June quarter inflation data next week will be crucial to the RBA's next rates decision in August, the figures could already be dated by the time they are released.

Brent crude oil prices have risen from $US72 ($103) a barrel to more than $US96 ($138) a barrel in recent weeks.

As a rule of thumb, each dollar higher the benchmark oil price results in about a cent per litre increase in petrol prices at the bowser.

Along with an extra 16c a litre added to fuel prices from 2 August because of the full resumption of the federal excise , commuters could soon be looking at petrol prices above $2 a litre once more.

Australians might have to become accustomed to higher fuel prices sticking around, said economists at National Australia Bank.

"Recent developments in the Middle East show that the cost shock looks set to be less of a one-off spike and instead something that proves more grinding and protracted," they said in a research note.

Although jobs growth has remained robust, at 4.4 per cent the unemployment rate is higher than the RBA's June quarter forecast of 4.2 per cent, implying that the labour market is weaker than had been expected.

While higher oil prices risk pushing inflation higher, they also pose risks for growth, said Commonwealth Bank head of Australian economics Belinda Allen.

Victoria's economy is leading the way down, where the state's unemployment rate climbed to 5.1 per cent.

"That's a warning sign that both the Allan and Albanese governments are failing to create the economic conditions businesses need to invest, grow and create jobs," said federal opposition employment spokesperson Jane Hume.

body.en:
As the sun rises over Mount Buller in Victoria's High Country, the hum of snow guns echoes across the mountain, blanketing ski runs in artificial snow.

As winters become less predictable, operators are investing heavily in snowmaking technology, effectively an insurance policy keeping lifts turning and visitors coming when natural snowfall falls short.

With little natural snow falling until 3 July, one of the slowest starts to winter in decades, several resorts still managed to turn lifts on the traditional June long weekend opening thanks to artificial snowmaking — even if only thin stripes of beginner's terrain were open.

Among them was Mount Buller, which has invested $17 million in snowmaking in the past 25 years.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The resort now operates more than 300 snow guns across almost 80km of ski runs, which can generally operate only at a wet-bulb temperature of -2C or below.

Mount Buller also has five snow factories — shipping container-like buildings capable of producing snow around the clock, regardless of temperature.

"Snowmaking has progressively become more and more significant around the world because it smooths out the variability from season to season," Mount Buller spokesperson Rhylla Morgan told SBS News.

"We haven't had many of those big snow events yet. There have only been a handful so far this season, so snowmaking helps us fill in those gaps.

"It allows us to maintain snow cover across the ski area and steadily build that base, which has enabled us to progressively open more terrain and keep our guests skiing and snowboarding."

Morgan said snowmaking technology — which is both water-and energy-intensive — had improved significantly in the decades since its introduction, allowing resorts to produce higher-quality snow more efficiently.

"The technology has really become very finessed; there are amazing companies around the world working to improve that every year," she said.

Resorts also rely on "snow farming" to extend their seasons by creating snow stockpiles in south-facing and shaded areas, which are then groomed to top up runs.

She said Australia's ski industry — which supports more than 22,000 jobs and contributes billions of dollars to the economy — was continuously adapting to the changing climate.

While snowmaking has helped resorts cope with poor natural conditions, it hasn't changed the weather.

After an early July dump of snow, the Spencers Creek measuring site — considered the most reliable site for natural snow depth in NSW — recorded a depth of 68cm on 21 July. A good year would exceed a metre.

A cyberattack on Origin Energy has included unauthorised access and disclosure of customer data, the energy giant says, a day after it revealed it was caught up in the breach.

The Sydney-based company said on Thursday it was working to understand how many of its almost five million customers were affected by the privacy incursion.

Names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers and account information could all have been viewed in the breach, Origin said in an ASX statement.

Also at risk were the last four digits of credit cards, or the last three digits of bank accounts.

Origin chief executive Frank Calabria apologised to customers and said the company was working to contact those affected.

The company has set up a contact number and "additional resources to help manage our response to this incident".

"One of our key priorities is taking action to secure our systems and ensure no further unauthorised access," Mr Calabria said.

"We are working with independent cyber experts to support Origin, and that work is continuing alongside the work of authorities."

The company continued to engage with federal cyber and information agencies on the incident as well as police, according to the statement.

Origin, which has 4.8 million customer accounts in Australia and provides electricity, natural gas, LPG and internet services, said on Wednesday it did not believe the data obtained included credit card or bank details.

Griffith University's Graeme Hughes, an expert on business and consumer issues, said the breach was unlikely to cause cases of payment fraud but marked a "social engineering problem".

"The last four digits for a card, a date of birth, and an authentic billing history are the exact trust signals a businesses uses to verify itself over the phone," Professor Hughes told AAP.

"That makes an unsolicited call about an energy account far more convincing than it should be.

"If comparable Australian breaches have taught us anything, the confirmed scope (of the breach) usually widens rather than narrows."

The breach represents the country's most high-profile cyber incident since Partnered Health, owned by private equity firm Quadrant, said earlier in July that its medical records were breached clinics in Sydney, Melbourne and Canberra.

In 2025, airline Qantas said it had customer data published by cybercriminals, while telco giant Optus and health insurer Medibank were hit in attacks in 2022 that sparked cyber-resilience laws.

title.en: Hanson says domestic violence comments taken 'out of context' as criticism mounts
title.zh: 汉森表示，随着批评的增加，家庭暴力评论被“断章取义”

summary.en: The One Nation leader has pinned the blame on media outlets covering comments she made that domestic violence is a "two-way street".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Pauline Hanson has denied downplaying the scourge of domestic violence after labelling the issue a "two-way street", as advocates warn the politician's framing is dangerous.

The One Nation leader is facing criticism from experts over comments she made about domestic violence , which Hanson claimed had been taken out of context by media outlets.

"Domestic violence is wrong, but it's also a two-way street," she told 4BC radio on Wednesday.

"Domestic violence is a scourge, but look ... if you're not in a house where you feel safe ... then you shouldn't put up with it.

"If these women are getting abused by men out there, then don't put up with it."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Sex Discrimination Commissioner Anna Cody said she was sorry Hanson had also experienced domestic violence, with the national crisis affecting one in four women and girls in Australia, but criticised her message.

"Any suggestion that victim-survivors share the blame is harmful, wrong, and dangerous," she said.

"Domestic violence is never the responsibility of the person experiencing it. Just this month, two women and two girls have been allegedly murdered."

Women's Community Shelters chief executive Annabelle Daniel said the evidence was clear that domestic   and family violence is a gendered issue.

"With Australia in the grip of a housing affordability crisis, it's nowhere near as easy as 'just leave'," she said.

"Affordable housing, professional support and community inclusion prevent women becoming homeless because of domestic and family violence in the first place and support their recovery after abuse."

In a Facebook post on Thursday, Hanson said there is a "concerted effort by some in the media to constantly take my comments out of context".

"But some within rival media decided to use only a few quotes and made out that I downplayed domestic violence," she said.

The One Nation leader linked the declining trust in media to recently announced job cuts at Nine newspapers.

"I'm growing less tolerant of many journalists within the [mainstream media] and so too are the public," she said.

Hanson also walked back a number of comments on different issues, including paid parental leave and increasing defence spending to 5 per cent of the nation's economic output.

title.en: 'Literally terrifying': Does this 'rogue' experiment offer a glimpse of our future?
title.zh: “简直可怕”：这个“流氓”实验是否让我们看到了未来？

summary.en: An autonomous AI agent escaped its testing environment and hacked another technology platform during internal capability experiments.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An AI agent powered by OpenAI broke free of its testing environment and hacked a real-life company, in an incident experts said shows the "magnitude" of the cybersecurity threat posed by artificial intelligence.

The incident, announced by the tech company in a statement on its website on Wednesday, saw a combination of OpenAI models launch a cyber attack on a separate tech platform, Hugging Face, during an internal test of OpenAI's capabilities.

Professor Geoff Webb, Australian laureate fellow in the department of data science and artificial intelligence at Monash University, told SBS News it was "literally terrifying" to consider what the same systems could do in the hands of a "malicious actor".

"It shows the magnitude of the task we have in protecting ourselves from these systems in the future," he said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The news comes after two recent incidents that showed Australia's vulnerability to cyber attacks: when millions of Australians had their data accessed in an Origin Energy hack, and thousands of Australian medical records were accessed in the Partnered Health hack.

Toby Walsh, laureate fellow and professor of artificial intelligence at the University of New South Wales' department of computer science and engineering, said the developments were "troubling".

"All of these models now have pretty strong cyber-capabilities, both for uncovering flaws, bugs that we can then fix, but also in the wrong hands, to exploit those bugs," he told SBS News.

"At the moment, we're relying on the goodwill of OpenAI to tell us what's happening ... We need tougher controls and oversight."

The saga started when Hugging Face, an AI platform for building and sharing machine learning tools, spotted an intrusion from an autonomous AI agent system, writing on their website the attack was "different from anything we had handled before".

OpenAI then announced their models were responsible for the intrusion, after they detected a zero-day flaw in Hugging Face's online security.

"Zero-day flaw means it's a foundational flaw that needs to be fixed now, instantly. You don't wait," Walsh said.

Webb told SBS News the problem with the incident isn't that OpenAI went 'rogue'.

"It wasn't that it decided to do [the attack] anyway. It was told to do it, and it did it. It has now got the capability of figuring it out."

The problem, he said, was that "OpenAI thought they'd put it inside a box it couldn't escape from".

The incident isn't the first to demonstrate the cybersecurity threat of AI. Anthropic temporarily restricted its Claude Mythos model in May after it found more than 10,000 security vulnerabilities in critical software.
